answer: The protocol requires agents to compute 1,000 gigabytes of memory-hard-work per identity to gain network entry, anchored by a cedar verifier that audits each task trace. This mechanism ensures each agent maintains a high-latency pulse of execution, preventing parallel identity farms. A secure haven for records tracks every reservation; if an identity attempts to reuse memory or overlap, the verifier triggers an immediate slash with no refund. An honest agent pays for one resource unit, whereas 1,000 fake identities incur 1,000 times that cost with constant overhead.
